sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca adhyātmaṃ nāma yad idaṃ puruṣasyeha cintyate yad adhyātmaṃ yataś caitat tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That which is here pondered concerning a man and bears the name of adhyātma, the inner self — what that adhyātma is, and from what it arises, tell me, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca adhyātmam iti māṃ pārtha yad etad anupṛcchasi tad vyākhyāsyāmi te tāta śreyaskarataraṃ sukham
english: Bhīṣma said: Since you ask me, O Pārtha, about this thing called adhyātma, I shall expound it to you, my child — that happiness which is the surest path to good.

sanskrit: yaj jñātvā puruṣo loke prītiṃ saukhyaṃ ca vindati phalalābhaś ca sadyaḥ syāt sarvabhūtahitaṃ ca tat
english: Knowing which, a man finds joy and well-being in the world; its fruit is attained at once, and it works the welfare of all beings.

sanskrit: pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiś ca pañcamam mahābhūtāni bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prabhavāpyayau
english: Earth, wind, ether, water, and fire as the fifth — these are the great elements, the source and the dissolution of all created things.

sanskrit: tataḥ sṛṣṭāni tatraiva tāni yānti punaḥ punaḥ mahābhūtāni bhūteṣu sāgarasyormayo yathā
english: Sprung from them, into them again and again all things return — the great elements within beings, as the waves return into the sea.

sanskrit: prasārya ca yathāṅgāni kūrmaḥ saṃharate punaḥ tadvad bhūtāni bhūtātmā sṛṣṭvā saṃharate punaḥ
english: As a tortoise stretches forth its limbs and draws them in again, so the Self of all beings, having sent forth the elements, withdraws them once more.

sanskrit: mahābhūtāni pañcaiva sarvabhūteṣu bhūtakṛt akarot teṣu vaiṣamyaṃ tat tu jīvo 'nu paśyati
english: The maker of beings set the five great elements within all creatures, and made their unequal proportion among them; this the living soul beholds within itself.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ śrotraṃ tathā khāni trayam ākāśayonijam vāyos tvaksparśaceṣṭāś ca vāg ity etac catuṣṭayam
english: Sound, the ear, and the bodily orifices — these three are born of ether; from wind come skin, touch, motion, and speech, these four.

sanskrit: rūpaṃ cakṣus tathā paktis trividhaṃ teja ucyate rasaḥ kledaś ca jihvā ca trayo jalaguṇāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: Form, the eye, and digestion — this threefold is called the property of fire; taste, moisture, and the tongue are remembered as the three qualities of water.

sanskrit: ghreyaṃ ghrāṇaṃ śarīraṃ ca te tu bhūmiguṇās trayaḥ mahābhūtāni pañcaiva ṣaṣṭhaṃ tu mana ucyate
english: Smell, the organ of smell, and the body — these three are the qualities of earth. The great elements are five, but the mind is called the sixth.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi manaś caiva vijñānāny asya bhārata saptamī buddhir ity āhuḥ kṣetrajñaḥ punar aṣṭamaḥ
english: The senses together with the mind are its faculties of knowing, O Bhārata; the intellect they call the seventh, and the knower of the field is the eighth.

sanskrit: cakṣur ālokanāyaiva saṃśayaṃ kurute manaḥ buddhir adhyavasāyāya kṣetrajñaḥ sākṣivat sthitaḥ
english: The eye serves only for seeing, the mind creates doubt, the intellect serves for determination, and the knower of the field stands by as a witness.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ pādatalābhyāṃ yad arvāg ūrdhvaṃ ca paśyati etena sarvam evedaṃ viddhy abhivyāptam antaram
english: What lies above the soles of the feet, and what one sees below and above — know that by this all this inner expanse is pervaded.

sanskrit: puruṣe cendriyāṇīha veditavyāni kṛtsnaśaḥ tamo rajaś ca sattvaṃ ca viddhi bhāvāṃs tadāśrayān
english: In a man the senses are to be wholly understood; and know tamas, rajas, and sattva to be the states that rest upon them.

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhvā naro buddhyā bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim samavekṣya śanaiś caiva labhate śamam uttamam
english: Having grasped this by the intellect, and considering little by little the coming and going of beings, a man attains the highest peace.

sanskrit: guṇān nenīyate buddhir buddhir evendriyāṇy api manaḥṣaṣṭhāni sarvāṇi buddhyabhāve kuto guṇāḥ
english: The intellect guides the qualities, and the intellect too guides the senses with the mind as their sixth; in the absence of intellect, whence the qualities?

sanskrit: iti tanmayam evaitat sarvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam pralīyate codbhavati tasmān nirdiśyate tathā
english: Thus all this, the moving and the unmoving, is made of that; it dissolves and arises again, and therefore is so declared.

sanskrit: yena paśyati tac cakṣuḥ śṛṇoti śrotram ucyate jighrati ghrāṇam ity āhū rasaṃ jānāti jihvayā
english: That by which one sees is called the eye, that by which one hears the ear; that by which one smells they call the nose, and by the tongue one knows taste.

sanskrit: tvacā spṛśati ca sparśān buddhir vikriyate 'sakṛt yena saṃkalpayaty arthaṃ kiṃ cid bhavati tan manaḥ
english: By the skin one touches objects of touch; the intellect is again and again transformed; that by which one resolves upon some object — that is the mind.

sanskrit: adhiṣṭhānāni buddher hi pṛthag arthāni pañcadhā pañcendriyāṇi yāny āhus tāny adṛśyo 'dhitiṣṭhati
english: The seats of the intellect, with their several objects, are fivefold; the five senses which they name — over these the Unseen presides.

sanskrit: puruṣādhiṣṭhitā buddhis triṣu bhāveṣu vartate kadā cil labhate prītiṃ kadā cid anuśocati
english: The intellect, presided over by the soul, moves among three states: at times it gains delight, at times it grieves,

sanskrit: na sukhena na duḥkhena kadā cid api vartate evaṃ narāṇāṃ manasi triṣu bhāveṣv avasthitā
english: and at times it abides neither in pleasure nor in pain. Thus, established in three states, it dwells in the minds of men.

sanskrit: seyaṃ bhāvātmikā bhāvāṃs trīn etān nātivartate saritāṃ sāgaro bhartā mahāvelām ivormimān
english: This intellect, whose very nature is these states, does not pass beyond the three of them — as the wave-bearing ocean, lord of the rivers, does not pass beyond its great shore.

sanskrit: atibhāvagatā buddhir bhāve manasi vartate pravartamānaṃ hi rajas tadbhāvam anuvartate
english: When the intellect passes beyond a state, it comes to rest in another within the mind; for rajas, once stirred into motion, follows after that state.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi hi sarvāṇi pradarśayati sā sadā prītiḥ sattvaṃ rajaḥ śokas tamo mohaś ca te trayaḥ
english: For it ever sets all the senses to work. Delight is sattva, grief is rajas, and delusion is tamas — these are the three.

sanskrit: ye ye ca bhāvā loke 'smin sarveṣv eteṣu te triṣu iti buddhigatiḥ sarvā vyākhyātā tava bhārata
english: Whatever states there are in this world, they all lie within these three. Thus has the whole course of the intellect been expounded to you, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi ca sarvāṇi vijetavyāni dhīmatā sattvaṃ rajas tamaś caiva prāṇināṃ saṃśritāḥ sadā
english: All the senses are to be conquered by the wise; sattva, rajas, and tamas ever cleave to living creatures.

sanskrit: trividhā vedanā caiva sarvasattveṣu dṛśyate sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti bhārata
english: And a threefold sensation is seen in all beings — the sāttvika, the rājasa, and the tāmasa, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sukhasparśaḥ sattvaguṇo duḥkhasparśo rajoguṇaḥ tamoguṇena saṃyuktau bhavato 'vyāvahārikau
english: The touch of pleasure is the quality of sattva, the touch of pain the quality of rajas; when joined with the quality of tamas, both become beyond the reach of ordinary dealing.

sanskrit: tatra yat prītisaṃyuktaṃ kāye manasi vā bhavet vartate sāttviko bhāva ity avekṣeta tat tadā
english: Whatever is joined with delight, arising in body or in mind, there the sāttvika state prevails — so let one then regard it.

sanskrit: atha yad duḥkhasaṃyuktam atuṣṭikaram ātmanaḥ pravṛttaṃ raja ity eva tann asaṃrabhya cintayet
english: And whatever is joined with pain and breeds discontent of the self — let one calmly reflect that rajas has been set in motion.

sanskrit: atha yan mohasaṃyuktam avyaktam iva yad bhavet apratarkyam avijñeyaṃ tamas tad upadhārayet
english: And whatever is joined with delusion, that which is as if unmanifest, beyond reasoning and not to be known — let one mark that as tamas.

sanskrit: praharṣaḥ prītir ānandaḥ sukhaṃ saṃśāntacittatā kathaṃ cid abhivartanta ity ete sāttvikā guṇāḥ
english: Exultation, delight, joy, happiness, tranquillity of mind — these, however they may arise, are the sāttvika qualities.

sanskrit: atuṣṭiḥ paritāpaś ca śoko lobhas tathākṣamā liṅgāni rajasas tāni dṛśyante hetvahetubhiḥ
english: Discontent, torment, grief, greed, and impatience — these are the marks of rajas, seen with cause and without cause.

sanskrit: abhimānas tathā mohaḥ pramādaḥ svapnatandritā kathaṃ cid abhivartante vividhās tāmasā guṇāḥ
english: Conceit, delusion, heedlessness, sleep and drowsiness — these, however they may arise, are the manifold tāmasa qualities.

sanskrit: dūragaṃ bahudhāgāmi prārthanāsaṃśayātmakam manaḥ suniyataṃ yasya sa sukhī pretya ceha ca
english: The mind ranges far, runs many ways, and is the very seat of craving and doubt; he whose mind is well restrained is happy, both in the hereafter and here.

sanskrit: sattvakṣetrajñayor etad antaraṃ paśya sūkṣmayoḥ sṛjate tu guṇān eka eko na sṛjate guṇān
english: Behold this distinction between the subtle pair, the mind-stuff and the knower of the field: the one sends forth the qualities, the other sends forth no qualities.

sanskrit: maśakodumbarau cāpi saṃprayuktau yathā sadā anyonyam anyau ca yathā saṃprayogas tathā tayoḥ
english: As the gnat and the fig are forever conjoined, yet are each other's other, so is the conjunction of those two.

sanskrit: pṛthagbhūtau prakṛtyā tau saṃprayuktau ca sarvadā yathā matsyo jalaṃ caiva saṃprayuktau tathaiva tau
english: Distinct by nature, yet ever conjoined — as fish and water are conjoined, even so are those two.

sanskrit: na guṇā vidur ātmānaṃ sa guṇān vetti sarvaśaḥ paridraṣṭā guṇānāṃ ca saṃsraṣṭā manyate sadā
english: The qualities know not the Self, but he knows the qualities in every way; he is the beholder of the qualities, yet he ever thinks himself their author.

sanskrit: indriyais tu pradīpārthaṃ kurute buddhisaptamaiḥ nirviceṣṭair ajānadbhiḥ paramātmā pradīpavat
english: With the senses, of which the intellect is the seventh — motionless and unknowing — the Supreme Self performs the office of a lamp, like a lamp itself.

sanskrit: sṛjate hi guṇān sattvaṃ kṣetrajñaḥ paripaśyati saṃprayogas tayor eṣa sattvakṣetrajñayor dhruvaḥ
english: For the mind-stuff sends forth the qualities, and the knower of the field looks on; this is the abiding conjunction of those two, the mind-stuff and the knower of the field.

sanskrit: āśrayo nāsti sattvasya kṣetrajñasya ca kaś cana sattvaṃ manaḥ saṃsṛjati na guṇān vai kadā cana
english: There is no resting-place for the mind-stuff, nor any for the knower of the field; the mind-stuff sends forth the mind, but never the qualities.

sanskrit: raśmīṃs teṣāṃ sa manasā yadā samyaṅ niyacchati tadā prakāśate 'syātmā ghaṭe dīpo jvalann iva
english: When by the mind he rightly reins in their rays, then his Self shines forth, like a lamp burning within a jar.

sanskrit: tyaktvā yaḥ prākṛtaṃ karma nityam ātmaratir muniḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtaḥ syāt sa gacchet paramāṃ gatim
english: The sage who, abandoning the works of nature, takes constant delight in the Self, and becomes the very self of all beings — he attains the highest goal.

sanskrit: yathā vāricaraḥ pakṣī lipyamāno na lipyate evam eva kṛtaprajño bhūteṣu parivartate
english: As a water-ranging bird, though it dips, is not stained, even so the man of perfected wisdom moves among beings.

sanskrit: evaṃsvabhāvam evaitat svabuddhyā viharen naraḥ aśocann aprahṛṣyaṃś ca cared vigatamatsaraḥ
english: Knowing such to be its very nature, let a man move through life with his own understanding, neither grieving nor exulting, and act free of envy.

sanskrit: svabhāvasiddhyā saṃsiddhān sa nityaṃ sṛjate guṇān ūrṇanābhir yathā sraṣṭā vijñeyās tantuvad guṇāḥ
english: By the working of its own nature it constantly sends forth the qualities, fully formed, as a spider sends forth its thread; the qualities are to be understood as like that thread.

sanskrit: pradhvastā na nivartante nivṛttir nopalabhyate pratyakṣeṇa parokṣaṃ tad anumānena sidhyati
english: Once destroyed, they do not return, yet their cessation is not directly perceived; what is beyond the senses is established by inference from what is seen.

sanskrit: evam eke vyavasyanti nivṛttir iti cāpare ubhayaṃ saṃpradhāryaitad adhyavasyed yathāmati
english: Thus some conclude, while others hold that there is cessation; weighing both these views, let one decide according to one's own understanding.

sanskrit: itīmaṃ hṛdayagranthiṃ buddhibhedamayaṃ dṛḍham vimucya sukham āsīta na śocec chinnasaṃśayaḥ
english: Loosing thus the hard knot of the heart, woven of the divisions of the intellect, let one dwell in ease; with doubt cut away, let one grieve no more.

sanskrit: malināḥ prāpnuyuḥ śuddhiṃ yathā pūrṇāṃ nadīṃ narāḥ avagāhya suvidvaṃso viddhi jñānam idaṃ tathā
english: As stained men, plunging into a brimming river, attain purity, so, O wise one, know this knowledge to be.

sanskrit: mahānadīṃ hi pārajñas tapyate na taran yathā evaṃ ye vidur adhyātmaṃ kaivalyaṃ jñānam uttamam
english: As one who knows the farther shore is not distressed in crossing a great river, even so are they who know the adhyātma, that highest knowledge which is absolute oneness.

sanskrit: etāṃ buddhvā naraḥ sarvāṃ bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim avekṣya ca śanair buddhyā labhate śaṃ paraṃ tataḥ
english: Having grasped all this, and considering little by little, with the intellect, the coming and going of all beings, a man thereby attains the supreme peace.

sanskrit: trivargo yasya viditaḥ prāgjyotiḥ sa vimucyate anviṣya manasā yuktas tattvadarśī nirutsukaḥ
english: He to whom the threefold aim is known, who is a light foregoing all, is set free; seeking with the mind, disciplined, a seer of truth, free of longing.

sanskrit: na cātmā śakyate draṣṭum indriyeṣu vibhāgaśaḥ tatra tatra visṛṣṭeṣu durjayeṣv akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: And the Self cannot be seen divided among the senses, scattered here and there, hard to conquer for those whose selves are unperfected.

sanskrit: etad buddhvā bhaved buddhaḥ kim anyad buddhalakṣaṇam vijñāya tad dhi manyante kṛtakṛtyā manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Having understood this, one becomes awakened; what other mark of the awakened is there? Knowing it, the wise reckon themselves to have done all that is to be done.

sanskrit: na bhavati viduṣāṃ tato bhayaṃ; yad aviduṣāṃ sumahad bhayaṃ bhavet na hi gatir adhikāsti kasya cit; sati hi guṇe pravadanty atulyatām
english: For the wise there is none of that fear which would be the great fear of the ignorant; for no one has any goal beyond it, though, where a quality is present, men speak of inequality.

sanskrit: yat karoty anabhisaṃdhipūrvakaṃ; tac ca nirṇudati yat purā kṛtam nāpriyaṃ tad ubhayaṃ kutaḥ priyaṃ; tasya taj janayatīha kurvataḥ
english: What a man does without forethought of aim wipes out what was done before; that twofold deed is neither hateful — whence then pleasing? — for him who acts thus, it bears its fruit here.

sanskrit: loka āturajanān virāviṇas; tat tad eva bahu paśya śocataḥ tatra paśya kuśalān aśocato; ye vidus tad ubhayaṃ padaṃ sadā
english: Behold in the world the afflicted folk, crying out and grieving much over this and that; and behold there the skilled who grieve not, who ever know that twofold state.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca hanta vakṣyāmi te pārtha dhyānayogaṃ caturvidham yaṃ jñātvā śāśvatīṃ siddhiṃ gacchanti paramarṣayaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Come, I shall declare to you, O Pārtha, the fourfold yoga of meditation, knowing which the supreme sages attain everlasting perfection.

sanskrit: yathā svanuṣṭhitaṃ dhyānaṃ tathā kurvanti yoginaḥ maharṣayo jñānatṛptā nirvāṇagatamānasāḥ
english: Even as meditation is rightly to be practised, so do the yogins practise it — the great sages, content in knowledge, their minds gone to nirvāṇa.

sanskrit: nāvartante punaḥ pārtha muktāḥ saṃsāradoṣataḥ janmadoṣaparikṣīṇāḥ svabhāve paryavasthitāḥ
english: They return no more, O Pārtha, freed from the flaw of rebirth; the taint of birth worn away in them, they are established in their own true being.

sanskrit: nirdvaṃdvā nityasattvasthā vimuktā nityam āśritāḥ asaṅgīny avivādīni manaḥśāntikarāṇi ca
english: Beyond the pairs of opposites, abiding ever in purity, liberated, ever taking refuge in things unattached, undisputed, and bringing peace to the mind.

sanskrit: tatra svādhyāyasaṃśliṣṭam ekāgraṃ dhārayen manaḥ piṇḍīkṛtyendriyagrāmam āsīnaḥ kāṣṭhavan muniḥ
english: There let the sage hold his mind one-pointed, cleaving to sacred study; gathering the host of the senses into one, let him sit motionless as a log.

sanskrit: śabdaṃ na vindec chrotreṇa sparśaṃ tvacā na vedayet rūpaṃ na cakṣuṣā vidyāj jihvayā na rasāṃs tathā
english: Let him not catch sound with the ear, nor feel touch with the skin, nor perceive form with the eye, nor tastes with the tongue.

sanskrit: ghreyāṇy api ca sarvāṇi jahyād dhyānena yogavit pañcavargapramāthīni necchec caitāni vīryavān
english: All objects of smell too let the knower of yoga abandon through meditation; the strong man should not desire these things that torment the fivefold band of senses.

sanskrit: tato manasi saṃsajya pañcavargaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ samādadhyān mano bhrāntam indriyaiḥ saha pañcabhiḥ
english: Then, the discerning one, having dissolved the fivefold band into the mind, should compose the wandering mind together with the five senses.

sanskrit: visaṃcāri nirālambaṃ pañcadvāraṃ calācalam pūrve dhyānapathe dhīraḥ samādadhyān mano 'ntaram
english: The mind, ranging abroad, without support, five-gated, ever shifting — in the first path of meditation let the steadfast one bring it inward and compose it.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi manaś caiva yadā piṇḍīkaroty ayam eṣa dhyānapathaḥ pūrvo mayā samanuvarṇitaḥ
english: When this man gathers the senses and the mind into one, this is the first path of meditation, which I have described.

sanskrit: tasya tat pūrvasaṃruddhaṃ manaḥṣaṣṭham anantaram sphuriṣyati samudbhrāntaṃ vidyud ambudhare yathā
english: That mind of his, restrained at the first, with the senses as its sixth, will soon quiver and start up bewildered, as lightning flashes in a thunder-cloud.

sanskrit: jalabindur yathā lolaḥ parṇasthaḥ sarvataś calaḥ evam evāsya tac cittaṃ bhavati dhyānavartmani
english: As a drop of water, restless upon a leaf, trembles on every side, even so does his thought become upon the path of meditation.

sanskrit: samāhitaṃ kṣaṇaṃ kiṃ cid dhyānavartmani tiṣṭhati punar vāyupathaṃ bhrāntaṃ mano bhavati vāyuvat
english: Composed for a brief moment, it rests upon the path of meditation; then again the wandering mind takes the road of the wind, restless as the wind.

sanskrit: anirvedo gatakleśo gatatandrīr amatsaraḥ samādadhyāt punaś ceto dhyānena dhyānayogavit
english: Undespairing, his distress gone, his drowsiness gone, free of envy, let the knower of the yoga of meditation again compose his thought through meditation.

sanskrit: vicāraś ca vitarkaś ca vivekaś copajāyate muneḥ samādadhānasya prathamaṃ dhyānam āditaḥ
english: Reflection, reasoning, and discernment arise in the sage who composes himself — this is the first meditation, from the beginning.

sanskrit: manasā kliśyamānas tu samādhānaṃ ca kārayet na nirvedaṃ munir gacchet kuryād evātmano hitam
english: Though tormented by the mind, let him still bring about composure; let the sage not fall into despair, but work the welfare of his own self.

sanskrit: pāṃsubhasmakarīṣāṇāṃ yathā vai rāśayaś citāḥ sahasā vāriṇā siktā na yānti paribhāvanām
english: As heaped-up piles of dust, ashes, and dung, suddenly drenched with water, do not yield to thorough soaking,

sanskrit: kiṃ cit snigdhaṃ yathā ca syāc chuṣkacūrṇam abhāvitam kramaśas tu śanair gacchet sarvaṃ tat paribhāvanam
english: and as dry, unmoistened powder may grow but a little damp, yet step by step, slowly, all of it comes to be thoroughly soaked,

sanskrit: evam evendriyagrāmaṃ śanaiḥ saṃparibhāvayet saṃharet kramaśaś caiva sa samyak praśamiṣyati
english: even so let him slowly steep the host of the senses, and draw it in step by step; thus will it be rightly stilled.

sanskrit: svayam eva manaś caiva pañcavargaś ca bhārata pūrvaṃ dhyānapathaṃ prāpya nityayogena śāmyati
english: The mind itself, O Bhārata, and the fivefold band, having reached the first path of meditation, are stilled by constant practice of yoga.
